// Module
var code = `<h1>Response format</h1> <p>The response format determines which capabilities the AI provider must support for extra-model parsing and how reliably MVU can read the variable updates.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Chat message:</strong> Offers the widest compatibility and requires no additional provider features. Reliability depends on whether the model follows the requested format.</li> <li><strong>Tool call:</strong> Requires tools/function-calling support. It usually reduces interference from prose. If the target endpoint or model rejects tool calling, the request reports a clear error and does not fall back automatically.</li> <li><strong>Structured output:</strong> Requires JSON Schema structured-output support. <strong>Custom</strong> sources use the OpenAI-compatible <code>response_format.json_schema</code>; <strong>More</strong> sources encode it using the selected API's wire format. This is usually the best option for JsonPatch variable updates because the response is constrained to structured JSON.</li> <li><strong>Structured output (v4 compatible):</strong> For providers, such as dsv4f, that support JSON Object output but not JSON Schema structured output. This mode is available for <strong>Custom</strong> sources and for APIs under <strong>More</strong> that support JSON Object output.</li> </ul> <p>When <strong>More</strong> is selected, MVU optimistically sends tool-calling or structured-output requests using the selected API's wire format; it does not probe the target endpoint or model first. If the target rejects the request, MVU reports a clear error through toastr and does not downgrade. Choose a response format the target supports, or check the API type, URL, and model name.</p> <p>If your provider explicitly supports JSON Schema structured output, try <strong>Structured output</strong> first. If it supports only JSON Object output, use <strong>Structured output (v4 compatible)</strong>. You can also try <strong>Tool call</strong> when the provider supports tools/function calling; otherwise use <strong>Chat message</strong>.</p> `;
// Exports
export default code;
